author: Antonialock
body:
well thee are 9 spermidine transporters annotated by ISO/IBA, which will get an F-P link annotation?  https://www.pombase.org/term/GO:0015606

It is strange, this rule is specific to taphrinomycotina but I do not see any EXP annotations for pombe that spark the rule!

in any case I could make an IGI annotation for mfs1 and IMP for caf5 from this paper: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22840777/
is "xenobiotic detoxification by transmembrane export across the plasma membrane" an acceptable term?
"Although single gene deletion of mfs1+  did not increase drug sensitivity, deletions of bfr1+ and mfs1+ together did"
"Analysis of caf5Δ cells revealed multidrug sensitivity that was greater than that of wild-type cells"

..."These studies led to two ABC transporters (Bfr1 and Pmd1), two MFS pumps (Mfs1 and Caf5), and two transcription factors (Prt1 and Pap1) as the major contributors to fission yeast’s MDR response"

author: ValWood
body:
xenobiotic detoxification by transmembrane export across the plasma membrane
is a strange term name (mine, historical,  I think)

If a xenobiotic is exported, that is detoxification, so I don't think that needs to be in the label. It could be

"xenobiotic  export across the plasma membrane"
A process that reduces or removes the toxicity of a xenobiotic by exporting it outside the cell.

and still be a descendant of detoxification.
@pgaudet  what do you think?

author: Antonialock
source_title: NTR: regulation of xenobiotic export across the plasma membrane

author: pgaudet
body:
> If a xenobiotic is exported, that is detoxification, so I don't think that needs to be in the label. It could be


If I recall correctly, we wanted this to clearly be under detoxification. Sometime usage drifts if the term is not clear enough. But I don't have a very strong feeling one way of the other.

author: Antonialock
body: I guess a lot of things that COULD transport drugs, but arent really detoxification transporters in vivo, were annotated to the term...

author: pgaudet
body: Interesting. If it's toxic AND is not made by the cell (ie, is a xenobiotic), why else (than detoxification) would the cell export the compound?

author: Antonialock
body: ahh, I had an example  (#5898 ) where a bunch of mammalian transporters (probably of the type SLC22*) were annotated to xenobiotic transport, but the xenobiotic was just the thing used in the transport assay. I can't remember what in vivo substrate it was used instead of

author: ValWood
body:
>If I recall correctly, we wanted this to clearly be under detoxification. Sometime usage drifts if the term is not clear enough. But I don't have a very strong feeling one way of the other.

it would be under detoxification, and defined as detoxification though? This should be enough?
And other terms under detoxification are similar, for example

sulfite export across plasma membrane

this one doesn't mention detoxification in the def, but it should.

If a xenobiotic is exported from a cell, I assume it's always detoxification at some level?

author: pgaudet
body:
See @Antonialock 's example above. If you think this risks happening without 'detoxification' in the label, then sure. 
(but I think many curators (and users) dont look at the ontology structure and term definitions )
